incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-INC-9843 — queue_backlog > 90% for service/autoscaler-controller, rolling 5m spike. Auto-escalation enabled. https://pagerduty.example/PD-INC-9843

pagerduty: Incident created and assigned to oncall: maria (oncall). Priority: P1. Pager: maria.

maria (oncall): ack'd. I'm booting into the runbook now. will post first triage in 60s.

derek (sre): seeing the same in Grafana — request queue length jumped, throughput down ~3x. autoscaler API shows pending scale requests.

sanjay (infra): provider reports quota errors for node-attach in the last 7m: `QuotaExceeded: InsufficientNodes` in cloud.log. Could be hitting per-region vCPU quota.

keisha (eng-runtime): Noted. We're also seeing increased KV-cache misses, which amplifies load. Could be cold-start churn triggering more queues.

maria (oncall): quick mitigations: 1) escalate to infra for quota check, 2) force a manual scale-up of spare pool if possible, 3) disable low-priority batching for latency-sensitive routes. I'm doing 2 now.

ops-bot: Running command on dedicated-controlplane: `./infractl scale --pool autoscaler-spare --add 4 --reason "pd-9843 manual surge"`

ops-bot: Command started: job-id 8921.

ops-bot: Job 8921: provisioning nodes requested. provider API accepted, but 2 nodes failed with `AttachTimeout`.

maria (oncall): Derek, can you check controller logs and confirm whether scale requests are queuing or being dropped?

derek (sre): tailing controller logs:```
I0325 14:07:03 autoscaler controller: enqueue scale request for pool autoscaler-main size 12 -> 20
E0325 14:07:06 provider: failed to create instance: QuotaExceeded: InsufficientNodes
W0325 14:07:10 autoscaler controller: retrying scale request (attempt 3)
E0325 14:07:20 autoscaler controller: backlog > threshold, rejecting new tasks
```

maria (oncall): OK that matches. Provider quota blocks are primary. Sanjay, any ETA from cloud team?

sanjay (infra): I've opened a quota increase with provider (case 65219). They replied ETA ~ 25-30m for vCPU raise. Meanwhile we can: a) reassign lower-priority workloads to another region, b) enable burst-capacity (if allowed), or c) evict best-effort jobs to free capacity.

keisha (eng-runtime): We can reduce per-request concurrency by lowering batch window and forcing immediate flush on critical routes. That will increase requests/sec but reduce queue length. I'll push a quick config change to routing: `service.routes["gen-critical"].batch.window_ms = 10`

maria (oncall): Do it. Also enable aggressive KV cache for warm prefixes: `kvcache.pin=true` for top 5 routes. Keisha, can you push a traffic-split to divert 20% of load to fallback model-quantized variant to lower node pressure?

keisha (eng-runtime): Pushing config now. Deploying canary split: `trafficctl split set --route gen-critical --variant quant-v2 --pct 20` -> ok, canary applied.

ops-bot: Node provisioning job 8921: 2 nodes active, 2 failed, 0 available. Autoscaler pool now reports `capacity=14/20` (effective).

maria (oncall): Manual scale-up successful for +2 active. Still short of target. Queue length drifting down slowly. Customers seeing elevated 429s for a subset of requests — ops has flagged SLOs.

derek (sre): I've applied temporary queue throttle at ingress for non-SLAs: `rate-limit: 100rps` for /v1/embeddings non-critical. This reduced pressure by ~15%.

maria (oncall): PagerDuty: ack -> acknowledged by maria at 14:09 UTC. If provider quota ETA holds, estimated full recovery when nodes are up and controller retries succeed.

pagerduty: PD-INC-9843 acknowledged by maria (oncall). Escalation locked.

keisha (eng-runtime): Noting an error pattern where the autoscaler controller's retry backoff is exponential and collides with provider throttling. I'll open a PR to add jitter + linear retry for quota errors. For immediate relief, lowering retry backoff to 5s helped one pending request proceed.

maria (oncall): Customer impact summary (preliminary): - Elevated latency and 429s for ~8% of live traffic 14:02–14:12 UTC. Affected tenants: prod-cust-11, prod-cust-47 (high), minor errors across other tenants. We're flagging for CS.

sanjay (infra): Provider update: quota increase approved for 12 vCPUs in region-1, ETA ~ 12 minutes. They will auto-provision nodes on approval.

maria (oncall): Great. Keisha, after provider nodes appear, coordinate with Derek to re-run controller retries and validate queue drain. Keep the 20% quant split for 15m post-recovery, then revert if stable.

keisha (eng-runtime): Will monitor. Adding alert to console for queue_length < 30 for 5m to mark recovery.

ops-bot: Provider webhook: quota increase applied at 14:21 UTC. New nodes provisioning.

ops-bot: Node provisioning complete: +6 nodes active. Autoscaler pool capacity 20/20.

derek (sre): Controller retries succeeded, backlog drained to baseline. No further scale errors in logs.

maria (oncall): Verified customer-facing metrics: 429 rate returned to baseline within 3m of nodes becoming active. Marking incident as mitigated.

pagerduty: PD-INC-9843 status changed to: Mitigated.

maria (oncall): Quick postmortem notes: root cause = region vCPU quota exhausted during sudden traffic spike + autoscaler blocked by provider QuotaExceeded errors. Contributing factors: no pre-warm spare for this region, controller retry/backoff exacerbated queue backlog, some routes had large batch windows increasing queue pressure.

maria (oncall): Follow-ups: 1) request permanent vCPU buffer for region-1 (sanjay) 2) PR to adjust retry/backoff for quota errors (keisha) 3) add runbook step to divert non-SLA traffic automatically (derek/keisha) 4) evaluate autoscaler prewarm to keep 2 warm nodes per region (product/infra). I'll file the incident ticket with timeline and assign action owners.

keisha (eng-runtime): filing PR and linking the incident ticket.

derek (sre): I'll coordinate the runbook update and CS update.

sanjay (infra): I'll follow up with provider to confirm buffer and quota monitoring alerting.

maria (oncall): handoff to next oncall in 30m. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident thread closed for PD-INC-9843 at 14:38 UTC (mitigated).
